# TD-6: Real UTD Dining locations and menu items

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Decided by:** Team 9 (the team agreed; approved by Rafael Amador, project manager)
- **Changes:** Supersedes A-16 (stub feed with two placeholder locations and placeholder items). FR-8, UC-1 "Browse Campus Dining Menu".

## Decision
1. The dining feed must serve the real UTD Dining locations and items in `spec/06-utd-dining/utd-dining-menus-2026-11-16.json`: Dining Hall West, Chick-fil-A, Panda Express, The Halal Shack, Firehouse Subs, Taco Bell Cantina and Starbucks (54 items). Use the item names, serving sizes and nutrition numbers exactly as given. Remove the old placeholder locations and items ("Dining Hall", "Campus Store").
2. Every item in that file was on UTD Dining's official menu site (Dine On Campus, linked from services.utdallas.edu/dining/menus/) for Monday, Nov 16, 2026. The source URL is listed per location. Show the building next to each location name.
3. Where the source publishes only calories (null fat/carbs/protein), store and show the macros as "not published"; do not invent numbers, and daily totals must still work (count them as 0 g for macro totals, and say so in ASSUMPTIONS.md).
4. Keep it a stub of the external "UTD Dining (menu data)" actor (no live calls to Dine On Campus); only its data changes. Existing meal entries that point at removed placeholder items may be cleared when the demo data is reset.
5. The demo data (TD-2) should use some of these real items in alice's and bob's meal history.

## Why
The team wanted the dining feature to show places students can actually eat on campus, with items that are actually sold there.

# CometFit server image (optional; README also shows running it with Maven directly).
FROM maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY pom.xml .
RUN mvn -q -B dependency:go-offline
COPY src ./src
RUN mvn -q -B -DskipTests package

FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /src/target/cometfit-server-*.jar app.jar
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]

1	# CometFit local stack. Start everything from the app/ folder with:   docker compose up --build
2	#   db     = MySQL 8.4, the "Encrypted Database" of D1 §5.3.2. Product and image from the team repo code
3	#            (spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md "MySQL for database operations", db/docker-compose.yml `mysql:8.4`).
4	#   server = CometFit REST server (API gateway, auth gateway, services; D1 §5.3.2).
5	# Fresh demo data: docker compose down -v   (deletes the database volume), then up again.
6	services:
7	  db:
8	    image: mysql:8.4
9	    environment:
10	      MYSQL_DATABASE: cometfit
11	      MYSQL_USER: cometfit
12	      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
13	      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-root}
14	    ports:
15	      - "3306:3306"
16	    volumes:
17	      - cometfit-mysql:/var/lib/mysql
18	    healthcheck:
19	      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "localhost", "-u", "cometfit", "-p${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}"]
20	      interval: 3s
21	      timeout: 3s
22	      retries: 30
23	
24	  server:
25	    build: ./server
26	    depends_on:
27	      db:
28	        condition: service_healthy
29	    environment:
30	      DB_URL: jdbc:mysql://db:3306/cometfit
31	      DB_USER: cometfit
32	      DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
33	      COMETFIT_DATA_KEY: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:-Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
34	      COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:-dev-integration-key}
35	      COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO: ${COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO:-true}
36	    ports:
37	      - "8080:8080"
38	
39	volumes:
40	  cometfit-mysql:

# CometFit local stack. Start everything from the app/ folder with:   docker compose up --build
#   db     = MySQL 8.4, the "Encrypted Database" of D1 §5.3.2. Product and image from the team repo code
#            (spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md "MySQL for database operations", db/docker-compose.yml `mysql:8.4`).
#   server = CometFit REST server (API gateway, auth gateway, services; D1 §5.3.2).
# Fresh demo data: docker compose down -v   (deletes the database volume), then up again.
services:
  db:
    image: mysql:8.4
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: cometfit
      MYSQL_USER: cometfit
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}

/** Settings-style row with a chevron (Account prototype). Tapping toggles an inline panel. */
export function ListRow({
  title, subtitle, open, onPress, danger, last, testID,
}: { title: string; subtitle?: string; open?: boolean; onPress: () => void; danger?: boolean; last?: boolean; testID?: string }) {
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={onPress} style={[s.listRow, last && !open ? null : s.listRowLine]} accessibilityRole="button" testID={testID}>
      <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
        <Text style={[s.listRowTitle, danger ? { color: colors.bad } : null]}>{title}</Text>
        {subtitle ? <Text style={s.small}>{subtitle}</Text> : null}
      </View>
      <Text style={s.chevron}>{open ? '⌄' : '›'}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}

/** Ranked row of a leaderboard ("01  starryskies23  2,500 ml"); the student's own row is highlighted green. */
export function RankRow({ rank, name, value, color, me }: { rank: number; name: string; value: string; color?: string; me?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <View style={[s.rankRow, me && s.rankRowMe]}>
      <Text style={s.rankNo}>{String(rank).padStart(2, '0')}</Text>
      <Text style={[s.rankName, me && { fontWeight: '700' }]} numberOfLines={1}>{me ? 'You' : name}</Text>
      <Text style={[s.rankValue, { color: color ?? colors.heading }]}>{value}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

/** Square letter badge of a log entry ("F" food in orange, "W" water in blue). */
export function LetterBadge({ letter, kind }: { letter: string; kind: 'food' | 'water' }) {
  return (
    <View style={[s.letter, { backgroundColor: kind === 'food' ? colors.foodBg : colors.waterBg }]}>
      <Text style={{ color: kind === 'food' ? colors.food : colors.water, fontWeight: '700' }}>{letter}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

/** Thousands separator as in the prototype ("1,250"). */
export function fmt(n: number): string {
  return Math.round(n).toLocaleString('en-US');
}

content.content:
1	# Assumptions
2	
3	Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
4	team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
5	Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).
6	
7	A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
8	---|---|---|---
9	A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
10	A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
11	A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
12	A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
13	A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
14	A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. # Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"

# Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. Session lifetime and TOTP parameters unchanged. See A-39.**
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings **SUPERSEDED for the seeded demo accounts only by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-2.md`: alice and bob start with all four sharing flags on. Real new accounts keep everything off (this row still applies to them). See A-40.**
A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. Points come only from visits and steps, so a friend appears (and their points show in their stats) only if they share visits or steps. | D1 UC-3 "View Leaderboard"; NFR Legislative-Privacy; Prop §7 leaderboard
A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope
A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec
A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT
A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)
A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Unlinking keeps history. In the browser, the OS permission prompt and the wearable are simulated (client `FakeSmartDevice`). Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability
A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2
A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3
A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security

A-34 | (stage 2) How the team's WATER_LOG table and LogWater unit fit the app's schema: column names, user id type, and what "fullName" is (team USERS has firstName/lastName; the class diagram User has only displayName) | Table `water_log(id, user_id BIGINT -> users.id, amount FLOAT(24) liters, logged_at DEFAULT now)`: the team's columns in this schema's snake_case and with the users key type (the team's `userId VARCHAR(64)` cannot reference an INT/BIGINT key). A-39 | (stage 2) TD-1 details: how the authenticator app is opened, what "larger screen" means, how a device is remembered | "Add to authenticator app" opens the standard `otpauth://totp/CometFit:<username>?secret=…&issuer=CometFit` link (account filled in); if nothing opens, the app says to use "Copy setup key". The setup key stays visible as selectable text. QR shown when the window is at least 768 px/dp wide. "Remember this device for 30 days" is a checkbox next to the code field. When checked and the code is valid, the server issues a random 256-bit device token, stores only its SHA-256 hash with a 30-day expiry, and the client keeps the token per username (browser localStorage, phone secure store). A remembered sign-in still needs the password, does not extend the 30 days, and only works for the same user. Changing the password forgets all remembered devices. A login with neither code nor device token is rejected as a malformed request (400) before the password is checked; every credential failure still gets one generic 401 message (A-31). | TD-1; D1 NFR Security; A-3, A-6, A-31 **SUPERSEDED in part by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-5.md`: (a) the code field and the "Remember this device for 30 days" checkbox are no longer on the sign-in screen; sign-in asks username + password only, and the code + checkbox are on a second "Verify it's you" screen shown only when the device is not remembered (TD-5 (1), (2)); (b) the 400 "neither code nor device token" rule is gone: the password step without a remembered device returns 200 with a single-use challenge and no session (TD-5 (2)), see A-42; (c) "QR shown when the window is at least 768 px/dp wide" is replaced by "QR on every screen size" at the setup step (TD-5 (3)). The history is written only when both students are newly created, so restarting the server does not duplicate it; for a clean demo, reset the database (`docker compose down -v`). | TD-2; D1 UC-3, SD-3; A-14, A-20, A-21
A-41 | (stage 2) Proposal feature not carried into D1/D2 requirements: "a map showing the different and closest areas to refill their water" | **Intentionally excluded** (decided by the team in `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-3.md`): out of scope for this version; no map, location or refill-station feature is built. FR-6 water logging is unaffected. | Prop §3 Project Objectives; D1/D2 FR-1..FR-8, UC-1..UC-4; TD-3
A-42 | (stage 3) TD-5 "short-lived, single-use challenge": how long it lives, how many wrong codes it allows, how it is sent | `POST /api/auth/login` {username, password, deviceToken?} returns either a session (remembered device) or `verificationRequired: true` + a random 256-bit `challengeId` and no token. `POST /api/auth/verify` {challengeId, totpCode, rememberDevice} completes it. Sign-in challenge lives 5 minutes; the setup challenge after Register 15 minutes (time to install Duo Mobile and scan). Deleted on success (single-use) and after 5 wrong codes; a wrong code before that keeps it so the user can retype. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored (table `login_challenges`); expired rows are purged hourly with sessions. Every failure (unknown/expired/used challenge, wrong code, wrong password) is the same generic 401 (A-31). | TD-5 (2), (5); D1 §5.2 AuthService; NFR Security
A-43 | (stage 3) TD-5 (3) registration: does the account exist before the first code is entered; what if the user leaves the setup screen | The account is created when Register is pressed (A-3, unchanged); Register returns the setup key / otpauth link and a setup challenge but no session. Entering the first valid code on "Set up two-step verification" completes the challenge and signs the user in (the "Remember this device" checkbox is offered there too). If the user leaves before that, they sign in later with password and get "Verify it's you"; the QR is not shown again (the secret is only returned once, NFR Security) — re-showing it would need an account-recovery feature the spec does not have. | TD-5 (3); A-3; NFR Security
A-44 | (stage 3) TD-4 names the colors but not exact values, fonts or sizes; the prototype logo is an image that is not in `spec/` | Hex values read off the PNGs: background #F6F6F1, dark green #1D4B35, orange #EF8E3A, food orange-brown #B5561D, water blue #2F6FED, light green #E4ECE2; white cards with 16 px radius; system font (the prototype font is not named). The logo is drawn as the "CometFit" wordmark in dark green (no image asset is in `spec/`). | TD-4 §1; `spec/05-ui-prototype/*.png`
A-45 | (stage 3) The Dashboard mixes data of two modules (daily summary = NUTRITION, UREC check-in/streak = ACTIVITY), but FR-5 disables modules one at a time | The Dashboard tab itself is never blocked; each part shows its own maintenance notice when its module is off, so the rest keeps working (FR-5). | TD-4 §2; FR-5; A-11
A-46 | (stage 3) Prototype sign-in elements with no matching FR/UC: "Sign in with Microsoft", "use your school email ending in @utdallas.edu", "By signing in, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" | Not built (TD-4 §3): sign-in is the CometFit username + password (A-3, A-4); the subtitle says so instead of the school-email text; no Terms/Privacy pages exist in `spec/`, so the footer keeps the existing general-wellness note. The layout (wordmark, centered title + subtitle, one wide button, small grey footer) follows the prototype. The "Verify it's you" and "Set up two-step verification" screens are not in the prototype; they use the same layout. | TD-4 §3; TD-5; `spec/05-ui-prototype/1-sign-in.png`
A-47 | (stage 3) What Week and Month on Food & Water show (the prototype only shows Today), with no server change allowed | Week = the last 7 local days, Month = the last 30, each ending today. Built from the existing `GET /api/nutrition/summary?date=` (one call per day): average calories and water per day, total calories, number of days the water goal was reached, and a per-day list. Today keeps the prototype layout; its "+ 250 ml" button is "+ <bottle size> ml" (one refill, A-8), the half-bottle and liters/gallons entry are behind "Other amount (L / gal)", and "+ Log food" opens the three meal-entry ways (manual, photo, dining menu). Macros (FR-2) and each meal's source stay visible in Today's log. | TD-4 §1-3; FR-2, FR-6, FR-8; UC-1; A-8, A-36
A-48 | (stage 3) The prototype's Social screen ranks friends by "Water · today", "Calories logged · today" and "Check-in streaks", but the server's leaderboard ranks by points only (A-21), friends' streaks are not in the friend stats (only `visitsThisWeek`), and no server change is allowed | The Water and Calories boards are built on the client from each friend's consented stats (`GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`) plus the student's own daily summary; a friend who does not share that field is left out (NFR Legislative-Privacy). "Check-in streaks" becomes "UREC visits · last 7 days" (consented `visitsThisWeek`). The server's points leaderboard (UC-3 "View Leaderboard") is kept as a fourth card. Friends list (stats, remove), friend requests and user search (FR-3) stay on Social below the boards; sharing settings moved to Account (TD-4 §2). | TD-4 §1-2; UC-3, SD-3; FR-3; A-21, A-30
A-49 | (stage 3) The prototype Dashboard's "current streak", "next milestone", "This week" row, "Total visits" and "Personal best" have no FR/UC definition | Computed on the client from the visit history (`GET /api/activity/visits`, FR-7), in the device's local time: a day counts if it has at least one UREC check-in ("One check-in per day counts toward your streak", prototype; same rule as points, A-20). Current streak = consecutive days ending today, or ending yesterday if the student has not checked in yet today. Personal best = longest such run. Total visits = all recorded visits. This week = Monday..Sunday (✓ = visited, orange ring = today not yet visited, showing the day number it would become, – = missed/future). Milestones every 5 days; the five bars show progress inside the current block of 5. "Check in at UREC" uses the existing stub card reader (A-12, A-27). The daily summary (calories, water, steps, macros, heart rate, low-water message) sits below as a "Today" card. | TD-4 §2; `spec/05-ui-prototype/2-dashboard.png`; UC-2, SD-2, FR-7; UC-1; A-20
A-50 | (stage 3) Prototype Activities elements with no FR/UC: "+ Log exercise" with workouts / active minutes / calories burned, "Upcoming classes" (Pilates, yoga), "Completed" workouts | No exercise-log, class schedule or calories-burned data exists in the spec, so none is invented (TD-4 §3). UREC visits (with "Check in at UREC"), recent points and smart devices follow in the same card style. | TD-4 §2-3; `spec/05-ui-prototype/5-activities.png`; UC-2, FR-4, FR-7
A-51 | (stage 3) Prototype Account rows: "Personal information — Edit name, birthday & campus", "Email & password", "Daily goals & units", "Notifications", "Privacy & data", "Terms of service", "Help & support", "Delete account" | Kept where the app has the feature, each opening its panel inline: Personal information (display name, public profile; no birthday or campus field exists in the class diagram), Email & password (email shown, change password), Daily goals & units (calorie, water, step goals, bottle size, NFR Safety warnings), Privacy & data (= the UC-3 sharing settings, TD-4 §2). Left out (no FR/UC, TD-4 §3): Notifications (Prop excludes push notifications), Terms of service, Help & support, Delete account. Section "SUPPORT & LEGAL" is named "PRIVACY & SECURITY" because only those rows remain. "Version 1.0" is the client package version. | TD-4 §2-3; `spec/05-ui-prototype/6-account.png`; FR-3; UC-3; NFR Security, Safety; Prop §4

lines: A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"

A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)

# Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). # CometFit — local setup and demo guide

CometFit (SE 3354 Team 9) is a student health-tracking app: meals and water (UC-1), activity and UREC visits (UC-2),
friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal,
Deliverable 1, the Deliverable 2 draft, the team's water-logging unit code, team decisions TD-1..TD-5 and the team's Figma prototype screens (all in `../spec/`). `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
that had to be filled.

```
app/
├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
└── docker-compose.yml MySQL 8.4 database + the server
```

The architecture follows Deliverable 1 §5.3 (client-server): the mobile client talks to one REST API, and every call
goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
the end of this file.

---

## 1. Install prerequisites

| Tool | Version used | Check with |
|---|---|---|
| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
| Docker Desktop | recommended (MySQL + server) | `docker version` |

Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 4, option B).

## 2. Install dependencies

```bash
# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
cd app/server
mvn -DskipTests package

# client
cd ../client
npm install
```

## 3. Configure environment variables

Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.

### Server (`app/server`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit-mysql` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
| `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `root` | MySQL root password (docker-compose only) |
| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
| `COMETFIT_REMEMBER_DEVICE_DAYS` | `30` | How long "Remember this device" skips the 6-digit code (TD-1) |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |

### Client (`app/client`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |

To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).

## 4. Run the project locally

### Start the database and server

**Option A — everything in Docker (recommended)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up --build        # MySQL 8.4 on localhost:3306 + the server on localhost:8080
```

Add `-d` to run it in the background. The server waits until MySQL is healthy. The first build downloads the Maven
dependencies inside the image, so it takes a few minutes.

**Option A2 — MySQL in Docker, server from Maven (for development)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up -d db
cd server
mvn spring-boot:run
```

**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database in MySQL mode)**

```bash
cd app/server
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2
```

Flyway creates the schema on first start (`V1` schema, `V2` water log in liters, `V3` remembered devices, `V4` sign-in
challenges for TD-5). The server
is ready when <http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`.

**Start the demo over with clean data** (removes everything, including test leftovers, then re-seeds the demo accounts):

```bash
cd app
docker compose down -v           # -v deletes the MySQL volume
docker compose up --build
```

With option B, stop the server and delete `app/server/data/` instead. *(Upgrading from the stage-1 PostgreSQL build:
the old `app_cometfit-db` volume and old H2 files are not used any more; delete them.)*

### Start the client

```bash
cd app/client
npm run web            # opens http://localhost:8081 in the browser
```

For a phone-like view in the browser, use the dev tools' device toolbar. On a real phone, run `npx expo start` and
open the app in Expo Go. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to your laptop's LAN address, for example
`http://192.168.1.20:8080`.

### Sign in

| Username | Password | TOTP secret | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alice` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITALICE234` | Student |
| `bob` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITBOBBY567` | Student |
| `dev` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITDEVADMIN` | Developer (admin dashboard) |

Sign-in has two steps (team decision TD-5):

1. **Sign in** — enter the username and password and press *Sign in*. No code is asked here.
2. **Verify it's you** — shown only when this browser/phone is not remembered. Enter the current 6-digit code from
   Duo Mobile (or any authenticator app with the secret above added), or print it with:

   ```bash
   node app/tools/totp.mjs COMETFITALICE234
   ```

   Tick **Remember this device for 30 days** to skip step 2 next time on this browser/phone (TD-1). The code is
   needed again on a new device, after 30 days, after a password change, or after *Account → Two-step verification →
   Forget this device*. The sign-in step expires after 5 minutes; if it does, press *Back to sign in*.

**Register** (from *New student? Create an account*) asks only for the account details. The next screen, **Set up
two-step verification**, shows a QR code to scan with Duo Mobile (on every screen size), plus **Add to authenticator
app** and **Copy setup key**. Enter the first 6-digit code and press *Finish setup* to sign in.

The demo students `alice` and `bob` are already friends, share all their stats, and have a week of meals, water,
steps, UREC visits and points (TD-2). Accounts you register yourself share nothing until you turn sharing on.

## 5. Run the tests

```bash
cd app/server && mvn test        # 63 API/unit tests on H2 (MySQL mode): Uc1..Uc4, WaterLogTest (team TC-1..TC-3),
                                 # RememberDeviceTest (TD-1), DemoDataTest (TD-2), TwoStepSignInTest (TD-5), security
cd app/client && npm test        # 26 client unit tests (Node test runner), incl. authFlow.test.ts (TD-5)
cd app/client && npm run typecheck
cd app/client && npx expo export --platform web   # production web build in app/client/dist (= npm run export:web)

# End-to-end over real HTTP against a running server (uses the demo accounts):
node app/tools/smoke.mjs http://localhost:8080
```

## 6. Demo script (about 5 minutes)

Start from clean demo data (`docker compose down -v`, then `docker compose up --build`).

The five tabs follow the team's Figma prototype (TD-4): **Dashboard, Food & Water, Activities, Social, Account**.

0. **Sign-in (TD-5, TD-1)** — Sign in as `alice` with username and password; *Verify it's you* asks for the code.
   Tick *Remember this device for 30 days* and *Verify*. Log out (Account) and sign in again: no second step. To
   show sign-up, register a new student: *Set up two-step verification* shows the QR code for Duo Mobile, *Add to
   authenticator app* and *Copy setup key*; enter the first code to finish.
1. **UC-1** — **Dashboard** shows the UREC streak and a *Today* card (calories, water, steps, low-water message). On
   **Food & Water**, tap *+ 500 ml* (one bottle refill). Tap *Other amount (L / gal)*, enter `0.3`, choose *gal* and
   tap *Add 1.13 L*: the app answers "Added 1.13L to Alice" (water is stored in liters). A negative amount is not
   accepted. Tap *+ Log food*: log a meal manually, then *Dining menu* → *Dining Hall* → *Add*, then *Photo (AI)* →
   pick any image, edit the estimate, *Confirm & save*. *Today's log* lists every entry; *Week* / *Month* show
   averages per day.
2. **Safety** — in **Account → Daily goals & units**, enter 800 kcal or 6000 ml and watch the warnings appear.
3. **UC-2** — **Activities** → *+ Connect smart device* → *Allow* (simulated health prompt) → *+ Sync activity from
   device*. Then *Check in at UREC* (here or on the Dashboard): +10 points, the visit appears in the history and the
   Dashboard streak updates.
4. **UC-3** — **Social**: the friends leaderboards (water, calories, UREC visits, points) show alice and bob (TD-2).
   Open bob's *Stats*. In **Account → Privacy & data** turn one of alice's sharing switches off, then in a second
   (private) browser window sign in as `bob` and see alice drop off that board and the stat show "Not shared". To
   show friend requests, register a new student and send `alice` a request (*Find people*).
5. **UC-4** — Sign in as `dev`. The developer dashboard shows uptime % and per-component status. Click *Simulate
   outage* on a component to see a downtime alert and an incident, then end it. *Disable* "Friends & Leaderboard" and
   switch to bob's window: the Social tab shows the maintenance notice while the other tabs keep working.
   *Re-enable* it.

Not built on purpose: the Proposal's water refill map (team decision TD-3, `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` A-41).

## 7. Stubs (external systems from the spec)

| External actor in the spec | Interface | Stub implementation |
|---|---|---|
| AI Food Recognition Service (UC-1) | `services/AIFoodService` | `stubs/FakeAIFoodService` — deterministic estimate from the image hash |
| UTD Dining menu data (UC-1, FR-8) | `services/UtdDiningFeed` | `stubs/StubUtdDiningFeed` — fixed sample menu for "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" |
| Smart Device pairing (UC-2) | `services/SmartDeviceGateway` | `stubs/FakeSmartDeviceGateway` — always pairs, except device ids starting with `FAIL` |
| Smart Device readings + health permission (UC-2) | client `src/smartDevice.ts` `SmartDeviceAdapter` | `FakeSmartDevice` — simulated steps / heart rate |
| UREC Card Reader (UC-2) | `POST /api/activity/visits` with the integration key | `stubs/FakeUrecCardReader` — the "Check in at UREC" buttons (Dashboard, Activities) |
| Monitoring Service (UC-4) | `POST /api/admin/health-check` with the integration key | `stubs/MonitoringAgentStub` — timer inside the server |
| Downtime alert channel (UC-4) | `services/AlertNotifier` | `stubs/LoggingAlertNotifier` — logs the alert and shows it on the dashboard |
| A real outage (demo only) | — | `stubs/OutageSimulator` — the "Simulate outage" button |

## 8. REST API overview

All endpoints except register, login and health need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

| Area | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Auth | `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/verify`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
| Profile (FR-3) | `GET/PUT /api/profile`, `PUT /api/profile/password`, `PUT /api/profile/goals` |
| Nutrition (UC-1) | `POST /api/nutrition/meals/photo`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/locations`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu?location=`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/meals`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/water`, `GET /api/nutrition/summary` |
| Activity (UC-2) | `POST/GET /api/activity/devices`, `DELETE /api/activity/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/activity/steps`, `GET /api/activity/records`, `POST /api/activity/visits` (reader), `GET /api/activity/visits`, `POST /api/activity/stub-reader/swipe` |
| Social (UC-3) | `GET /api/social/users/search?q=`, `GET /api/social/users/{id}`, `POST/GET /api/social/requests`, `POST /api/social/requests/{id}/accept\|decline`, `GET /api/social/friends`, `DELETE /api/social/friends/{id}`, `GET/PUT /api/social/consent`, `GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`, `GET /api/social/leaderboard` |
| Modules (FR-5) | `GET /api/modules`, `GET /api/modules/{id}` |
| Admin (UC-4) | `GET /api/admin/access`, `GET /api/admin/uptime?hours=`, `POST /api/admin/uptime/check-now`, `GET /api/admin/alerts`, `GET /api/admin/modules`, `POST /api/admin/modules/{id}/disable\|enable`, `POST /api/admin/health-check` (monitor), `POST /api/admin/stub/outage` |

Sign-in (stage 3, TD-5): `POST /api/auth/login` takes `username`, `password` and optional `deviceToken` (a remembered
device). It returns a session (`token`, `user`, `rememberedDevice: true`) only for a remembered device; otherwise
`verificationRequired: true` with a single-use `challengeId` (5 minutes) and **no** token. `POST /api/auth/verify`
takes `challengeId`, `totpCode` and optional `rememberDevice` and returns the session, plus `deviceToken` /
`trustedUntil` when the device was just remembered. `POST /api/auth/register` returns `totpSecret`, `otpauthUri` and a
`setupChallengeId` (15 minutes) that the first code completes through `/verify`. Every credential failure is the same
`401 "Invalid username, password or code"`. `POST /api/nutrition/water` takes `{"amount": 0.3, "isLiter": false}` (liters or gallons, team
`LogWater`) or `{"volumeMl": 500}`, and returns `message` (for example "Added 1.13L to Alice").

When a module is disabled, its endpoints answer `503 {"code":"MODULE_DISABLED"}` and the app shows a maintenance
notice.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Cannot reach the CometFit server"** in the app: the server isn't running, or `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is wrong.
- **"Invalid username, password or code" on Verify it's you:** the 6-digit code is wrong or expired, the laptop clock
  is off, or the sign-in step timed out (5 minutes) / had 5 wrong codes — press *Back to sign in* and start again.
- **Port 8080 already in use:** set `PORT=8090` before starting the server, and set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8090` for the client.
- **CORS error in the browser:** add the page's origin to `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **"Could not decrypt field":** `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` changed after the accounts were created. Restore the old key or reset the database.

## 8. REST API overview

All endpoints except register, login and health need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

| Area | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Auth | `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/verify`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
| Profile (FR-3) | `GET/PUT /api/profile`, `PUT /api/profile/password`, `PUT /api/profile/goals` |
| Nutrition (UC-1) | `POST /api/nutrition/meals/photo`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/locations`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu?location=`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/meals`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/water`, `GET /api/nutrition/summary` |
| Activity (UC-2) | `POST/GET /api/activity/devices`, `DELETE /api/activity/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/activity/steps`, `GET /api/activity/records`, `POST /api/activity/visits` (reader), `GET /api/activity/visits`, `POST /api/activity/stub-reader/swipe` |
| Social (UC-3) | `GET /api/social/users/search?q=`, `GET /api/social/users/{id}`, `POST/GET /api/social/requests`, `POST /api/social/requests/{id}/accept\|decline`, `GET /api/social/friends`, `DELETE /api/social/friends/{id}`, `GET/PUT /api/social/consent`, `GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`, `GET /api/social/leaderboard` |
| Modules (FR-5) | `GET /api/modules`, `GET /api/modules/{id}` |
| Admin (UC-4) | `GET /api/admin/access`, `GET /api/admin/uptime?hours=`, `POST /api/admin/uptime/check-now`, `GET /api/admin/alerts`, `GET /api/admin/modules`, `POST /api/admin/modules/{id}/disable\|enable`, `POST /api/admin/health-check` (monitor), `POST /api/admin/stub/outage` |

Sign-in (stage 3, TD-5): `POST /api/auth/login` takes `username`, `password` and optional `deviceToken` (a remembered
device). It returns a session (`token`, `user`, `rememberedDevice: true`) only for a remembered device; otherwise
`verificationRequired: true` with a single-use `challengeId` (5 minutes) and **no** token. `POST /api/auth/verify`
takes `challengeId`, `totpCode` and optional `rememberDevice` and returns the session, plus `deviceToken` /
`trustedUntil` when the device was just remembered. `POST /api/auth/register` returns `totpSecret`, `otpauthUri` and a
`setupChallengeId` (15 minutes) that the first code completes through `/verify`. Every credential failure is the same
`401 "Invalid username, password or code"`. `POST /api/nutrition/water` takes `{"amount": 0.3, "isLiter": false}` (liters or gallons, team
`LogWater`) or `{"volumeMl": 500}`, and returns `message` (for example "Added 1.13L to Alice").

When a module is disabled, its endpoints answer `503 {"code":"MODULE_DISABLED"}` and the app shows a maintenance
notice.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Cannot reach the CometFit server"** in the app: the server isn't running, or `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is wrong.
- **"Invalid username, password or code" on Verify it's you:** the 6-digit code is wrong or expired, the laptop clock
  is off, or the sign-in step timed out (5 minutes) / had 5 wrong codes — press *Back to sign in* and start again.
- **Port 8080 already in use:** set `PORT=8090` before starting the server, and set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8090` for the client.
- **CORS error in the browser:** add the page's origin to `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **"Could not decrypt field":** `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` changed after the accounts were created. Restore the old key or reset the database.

# CometFit — local setup and demo guide

CometFit (SE 3354 Team 9) is a student health-tracking app: meals and water (UC-1), activity and UREC visits (UC-2),
friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal,
Deliverable 1, the Deliverable 2 draft, the team's water-logging unit code, team decisions TD-1..TD-5 and the team's Figma prototype screens (all in `../spec/`). `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
that had to be filled.

```
app/
├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
└── docker-compose.yml MySQL 8.4 database + the server
```

The architecture follows Deliverable 1 §5.3 (client-server): the mobile client talks to one REST API, and every call
goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
the end of this file.

---

## 1. Install prerequisites

| Tool | Version used | Check with |
|---|---|---|
| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
| Docker Desktop | recommended (MySQL + server) | `docker version` |

Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 4, option B).

## 2. Install dependencies

```bash
# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
cd app/server
mvn -DskipTests package

# client
cd ../client
npm install
```

## 3. Configure environment variables

Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.

### Server (`app/server`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit-mysql` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
| `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `root` | MySQL root password (docker-compose only) |
| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
| `COMETFIT_REMEMBER_DEVICE_DAYS` | `30` | How long "Remember this device" skips the 6-digit code (TD-1) |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |

### Client (`app/client`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |

To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).

takes `challengeId`, `totpCode` and optional `rememberDevice` and returns the session, plus `deviceToken` /
`trustedUntil` when the device was just remembered. `POST /api/auth/register` returns `totpSecret`, `otpauthUri` and a
`setupChallengeId` (15 minutes) that the first code completes through `/verify`. Every credential failure is the same
`401 "Invalid username, password or code"`. `POST /api/nutrition/water` takes `{"amount": 0.3, "isLiter": false}` (liters or gallons, team
`LogWater`) or `{"volumeMl": 500}`, and returns `message` (for example "Added 1.13L to Alice").

When a module is disabled, its endpoints answer `503 {"code":"MODULE_DISABLED"}` and the app shows a maintenance
notice.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Cannot reach the CometFit server"** in the app: the server isn't running, or `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is wrong.
- **"Invalid username, password or code" on Verify it's you:** the 6-digit code is wrong or expired, the laptop clock
  is off, or the sign-in step timed out (5 minutes) / had 5 wrong codes — press *Back to sign in* and start again.
- **Port 8080 already in use:** set `PORT=8090` before starting the server, and set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8090` for the client.
- **CORS error in the browser:** add the page's origin to `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **"Could not decrypt field":** `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` changed after the accounts were created. Restore the old key or reset the database.

# CometFit — local setup and demo guide

CometFit (SE 3354 Team 9) is a student health-tracking app: meals and water (UC-1), activity and UREC visits (UC-2),
friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal,
Deliverable 1, the Deliverable 2 draft, the team's water-logging unit code, team decisions TD-1..TD-5 and the team's Figma prototype screens (all in `../spec/`). `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
that had to be filled.

```
app/
├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
└── docker-compose.yml MySQL 8.4 database + the server
```

The architecture follows Deliverable 1 §5.3 (client-server): the mobile client talks to one REST API, and every call
goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
the end of this file.

---

## 1. Install prerequisites

| Tool | Version used | Check with |
|---|---|---|
| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
| Docker Desktop | recommended (MySQL + server) | `docker version` |

Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 4, option B).

## 2. Install dependencies

```bash
# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
cd app/server
mvn -DskipTests package

# client
cd ../client
npm install
```

## 3. Configure environment variables

Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.

### Server (`app/server`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit-mysql` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
| `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `root` | MySQL root password (docker-compose only) |
| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
| `COMETFIT_REMEMBER_DEVICE_DAYS` | `30` | How long "Remember this device" skips the 6-digit code (TD-1) |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |

### Client (`app/client`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |

To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).

## 4. Run the project locally

### Start the database and server

**Option A — everything in Docker (recommended)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up --build        # MySQL 8.4 on localhost:3306 + the server on localhost:8080
```

Add `-d` to run it in the background. The server waits until MySQL is healthy. The first build downloads the Maven
dependencies inside the image, so it takes a few minutes.

**Option A2 — MySQL in Docker, server from Maven (for development)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up -d db
cd server
mvn spring-boot:run
```

**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database in MySQL mode)**

```bash
cd app/server
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2
```

Flyway creates the schema on first start (`V1` schema, `V2` water log in liters, `V3` remembered devices, `V4` sign-in
challenges for TD-5). The server
is ready when <http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`.

**Start the demo over with clean data** (removes everything, including test leftovers, then re-seeds the demo accounts):

```bash
cd app
docker compose down -v           # -v deletes the MySQL volume
docker compose up --build
```

With option B, stop the server and delete `app/server/data/` instead. *(Upgrading from the stage-1 PostgreSQL build:
the old `app_cometfit-db` volume and old H2 files are not used any more; delete them.)*

### Start the client

```bash
cd app/client
npm run web            # opens http://localhost:8081 in the browser
```

For a phone-like view in the browser, use the dev tools' device toolbar. On a real phone, run `npx expo start` and
open the app in Expo Go. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to your laptop's LAN address, for example
`http://192.168.1.20:8080`.

### Sign in

| Username | Password | TOTP secret | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alice` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITALICE234` | Student |
| `bob` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITBOBBY567` | Student |
| `dev` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITDEVADMIN` | Developer (admin dashboard) |

Sign-in has two steps (team decision TD-5):

1. **Sign in** — enter the username and password and press *Sign in*. No code is asked here.
2. **Verify it's you** — shown only when this browser/phone is not remembered. Enter the current 6-digit code from
   Duo Mobile (or any authenticator app with the secret above added), or print it with:

   ```bash
   node app/tools/totp.mjs COMETFITALICE234
   ```

   Tick **Remember this device for 30 days** to skip step 2 next time on this browser/phone (TD-1). The code is
   needed again on a new device, after 30 days, after a password change, or after *Account → Two-step verification →
   Forget this device*. The sign-in step expires after 5 minutes; if it does, press *Back to sign in*.

**Register** (from *New student? Create an account*) asks only for the account details. The next screen, **Set up
two-step verification**, shows a QR code to scan with Duo Mobile (on every screen size), plus **Add to authenticator
app** and **Copy setup key**. Enter the first 6-digit code and press *Finish setup* to sign in.

The demo students `alice` and `bob` are already friends, share all their stats, and have a week of meals, water,
steps, UREC visits and points (TD-2). Accounts you register yourself share nothing until you turn sharing on.

## 5. Run the tests

```bash
cd app/server && mvn test        # 63 API/unit tests on H2 (MySQL mode): Uc1..Uc4, WaterLogTest (team TC-1..TC-3),
                                 # RememberDeviceTest (TD-1), DemoDataTest (TD-2), TwoStepSignInTest (TD-5), security
cd app/client && npm test        # 26 client unit tests (Node test runner), incl. authFlow.test.ts (TD-5)
cd app/client && npm run typecheck
cd app/client && npx expo export --platform web   # production web build in app/client/dist (= npm run export:web)

# End-to-end over real HTTP against a running server (uses the demo accounts):
node app/tools/smoke.mjs http://localhost:8080
```

## 6. Demo script (about 5 minutes)

Start from clean demo data (`docker compose down -v`, then `docker compose up --build`).

The five tabs follow the team's Figma prototype (TD-4): **Dashboard, Food & Water, Activities, Social, Account**.

0. **Sign-in (TD-5, TD-1)** — Sign in as `alice` with username and password; *Verify it's you* asks for the code.
   Tick *Remember this device for 30 days* and *Verify*. Log out (Account) and sign in again: no second step. To
   show sign-up, register a new student: *Set up two-step verification* shows the QR code for Duo Mobile, *Add to
   authenticator app* and *Copy setup key*; enter the first code to finish.
1. **UC-1** — **Dashboard** shows the UREC streak and a *Today* card (calories, water, steps, low-water message). On
   **Food & Water**, tap *+ 500 ml* (one bottle refill). Tap *Other amount (L / gal)*, enter `0.3`, choose *gal* and
   tap *Add 1.13 L*: the app answers "Added 1.13L to Alice" (water is stored in liters). A negative amount is not
   accepted. Tap *+ Log food*: log a meal manually, then *Dining menu*: the 7 UTD Dining locations with their
   buildings (TD-6). Open *Dining Hall West (Andromeda Hall)* — calories only, macros "not published" — and *Add*
   *Italian Nachos*; the macro totals note that it counts as 0 g. Open *Chick-fil-A* to show an item with published
   macros. Then *Photo (AI)* → pick any image, edit the estimate, *Confirm & save*. *Today's log* lists every entry;
   *Week* / *Month* show averages per day. alice's and bob's earlier days are real UTD Dining items (TD-6 §5).
2. **Safety** — in **Account → Daily goals & units**, enter 800 kcal or 6000 ml and watch the warnings appear.
3. **UC-2** — **Activities** → *+ Connect smart device* → *Allow* (simulated health prompt) → *+ Sync activity from
   device*. Then *Check in at UREC* (here or on the Dashboard): +10 points, the visit appears in the history and the
   Dashboard streak updates.
4. **UC-3** — **Social**: the friends leaderboards (water, calories, UREC visits, points) show alice and bob (TD-2).
   Open bob's *Stats*. In **Account → Privacy & data** turn one of alice's sharing switches off, then in a second
   (private) browser window sign in as `bob` and see alice drop off that board and the stat show "Not shared". To
   show friend requests, register a new student and send `alice` a request (*Find people*).
5. **UC-4** — Sign in as `dev`. The developer dashboard shows uptime % and per-component status. Click *Simulate
   outage* on a component to see a downtime alert and an incident, then end it. *Disable* "Friends & Leaderboard" and
   switch to bob's window: the Social tab shows the maintenance notice while the other tabs keep working.
   *Re-enable* it.

Not built on purpose: the Proposal's water refill map (team decision TD-3, `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` A-41).

## 7. Stubs (external systems from the spec)

| External actor in the spec | Interface | Stub implementation |
|---|---|---|
| AI Food Recognition Service (UC-1) | `services/AIFoodService` | `stubs/FakeAIFoodService` — deterministic estimate from the image hash |
| UTD Dining menu data (UC-1, FR-8) | `services/UtdDiningFeed` | `stubs/StubUtdDiningFeed` — TD-6: the 7 UTD Dining locations / 54 items of `spec/06-utd-dining` (Monday 2026-11-16 menus, classpath copy `utd-dining/…json`), same menu every day, no live calls |
| Smart Device pairing (UC-2) | `services/SmartDeviceGateway` | `stubs/FakeSmartDeviceGateway` — always pairs, except device ids starting with `FAIL` |
| Smart Device readings + health permission (UC-2) | client `src/smartDevice.ts` `SmartDeviceAdapter` | `FakeSmartDevice` — simulated steps / heart rate |
| UREC Card Reader (UC-2) | `POST /api/activity/visits` with the integration key | `stubs/FakeUrecCardReader` — the "Check in at UREC" buttons (Dashboard, Activities) |
| Monitoring Service (UC-4) | `POST /api/admin/health-check` with the integration key | `stubs/MonitoringAgentStub` — timer inside the server |
| Downtime alert channel (UC-4) | `services/AlertNotifier` | `stubs/LoggingAlertNotifier` — logs the alert and shows it on the dashboard |
| A real outage (demo only) | — | `stubs/OutageSimulator` — the "Simulate outage" button |

## 8. REST API overview

All endpoints except register, login and health need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

| Area | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Auth | `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/verify`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
| Profile (FR-3) | `GET/PUT /api/profile`, `PUT /api/profile/password`, `PUT /api/profile/goals` |
| Nutrition (UC-1) | `POST /api/nutrition/meals/photo`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/locations`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/location-info` (TD-6: building, menu, source), `GET /api/nutrition/menu?location=`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/meals`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/water`, `GET /api/nutrition/summary` |
| Activity (UC-2) | `POST/GET /api/activity/devices`, `DELETE /api/activity/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/activity/steps`, `GET /api/activity/records`, `POST /api/activity/visits` (reader), `GET /api/activity/visits`, `POST /api/activity/stub-reader/swipe` |
| Social (UC-3) | `GET /api/social/users/search?q=`, `GET /api/social/users/{id}`, `POST/GET /api/social/requests`, `POST /api/social/requests/{id}/accept\|decline`, `GET /api/social/friends`, `DELETE /api/social/friends/{id}`, `GET/PUT /api/social/consent`, `GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`, `GET /api/social/leaderboard` |
